passages.provision_quote: “Race” is inclusive of traits historically associated with race, including, but not limited to, hair texture and protective hairstyles.
passages.note: The bill text prints the operative widening of the definition of race under the Education Code and the Fair Employment and Housing Act, but names no voter and shows the bill was authored by Mitchell.

rows.reasoning: The only record is Caballero's Aye on SB 188 (2019-2020), which widens the definition of race to include "traits historically associated with race, including, but not limited to, hair texture and protective hairstyles" — content that speaks to "strengthen civil rights enforcement and address systemic discrimination". The tally is "Ayes Count 37 Noes Count 0 NVR Count 1", a near-unanimous vote, and the bill is authored by Mitchell, so under V4.1 and the annex this vote cannot carry the chair without Caballero's authorship or her own words tying her to the provision.
